label: caiso 84 gas spot level
definition: CAISO KEEPER (caiso-80 recipe + the single delta caiso_citygate_spot_level=True): re-levels the CAISO gas hub overlay from the EIA N3050CA3 monthly citygate SURVEY (an LDC portfolio acquisition cost) onto the measured California Composite daily citygate SPOT the cost-based default energy bid prices the marginal unit at (rule-15 measured-series swap, zero new scalars; FINDING-caiso-winter-gas-level-2026-07-15). Closes the dominant WINTER over-pricing: 2023 Jan $222.0->$136.6 vs actual $129.7 (+71%->+5.3%), Feb $95.7->$68.1 vs $66.4 (+44%->+2.5%); C3a-2023 +32.5%->+11.9%; C3b-2023 0.562->passing; C3c-2023 667h->16h (>$200). The survey<spot shoulder months (Mar/Oct-2023) move UP toward actual, which a fit-chasing knob could not do (the structural tell). Promoted over caiso-80 on rule-1 structural-fidelity grounds (per-year measured data, the caiso-80 LOYO class). NOT-YET overall: the residual is now the summer soft-months (May/Jun) on the import-ladder M-regime lane (caiso-86 measured ladder refuted at the honesty gates 2026-07-15) plus C1 2024 CC +6.67 TWh from cheaper gas, C3c under-shoot, C4 gas 0.323.
market_story: CC_REGULAR: California's marginal combined-cycle prices its cost-based default energy bid off the DAILY SoCal/PG&E citygate spot index its fuel actually costs that day, not the monthly LDC acquisition-cost survey; in the Jan-2023 cold snap that spot ran ~$16.1/MMBtu (survey ~$28.08), so the efficient-CC clearing price is ~$130-137/MWh — the level DA/RT actually cleared at — and the fleet burns marginally more gas at the cheaper delivered fuel (the +6.7 TWh CC 2024 tick). Shoulder months (Mar/Oct) where the survey sat BELOW spot reprice UP toward actual, confirming a measured basis-source correction rather than a residual-fitted level.
